You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: H0162

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "alas! ah! — an exclamation of grief, dismay, or desperate appeal"
  Readable gloss: "Ahahh is one of the rawest sounds in the Hebrew Bible — a guttural cry erupting at moments of shock, grief, or pleading. Jephthah cries it upon seeing his daughter (Judg 11:35); Elisha's servant cries it when the axe head sinks into the Jordan (2 Kgs 6:5). Most characteristically it appears in the formula ahahh adonai YHWH ('alas, Lord GOD!'), a phrase of prophetic anguish used by Joshua (7:7), Gideon (Judg 6:22), Jeremiah, and Ezekiel. Spanish 'ah/ay,' French 'helas,' and German 'ach' each reach for their most visceral interjection."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "alas"
    Enriched: An interjection expressing acute distress, dismay, or anguished appeal to God. Occurs as a standalone cry of shock (Judg 11:35; 2 Kgs 6:5, 15) and in the formulaic address ahahh adonai YHWH ('alas, Lord GOD!'), found in Joshua, Judges, Jeremiah, and Ezekiel. Joel intensifies it with ahahh layyom, 'alas for the day!' (1:15). German 'ach' and French 'helas' mirror the raw emotive register.
    Existing Spanish translations: Ah, ah, ay, ¡Ah!, ¡Ay, ¡Ay!, ¡ah!
